usageNotice: Original synthetic research/demo sample. Every named contract, dependency, incident and review status is fictional; no real addresses, transactions, losses, exploit steps or verified security claims are provided. Not a production security intelligence dataset, audit, risk score or investment recommendation. MIT permits commercial reuse; research/demo describes intended use, not an added license restriction.

sources.title: Fictional dependency and review register
sources.excerpt: This invented register concerns three imaginary contracts. Lumen Vault has not undergone the fictional team's review and depends on Loom Ledger. Harbor Pool has undergone that team's review and also depends on Loom Ledger. Kite Reserve has not undergone that review and depends on Reed Rates instead. A review label is not a guarantee of safety. Shared dependency alone does not prove that Lumen has Harbor's weakness.

sources.title: Fictional Harbor tabletop incident
sources.excerpt: Harbor Tabletop is an invented incident exercise involving Harbor Pool. The exercise illustrates the abstract weakness Nested State Inconsistency, which the fictional scenario assigns to Harbor Pool. No executable contract, attack sequence, real incident date or monetary loss exists. The purpose is to connect incident, contract and weakness records for retrieval evaluation, not to teach exploitation.

sources.title: Fictional Loom dependency review
sources.excerpt: In this fictional review, Loom Ledger is affected by the abstract weakness Nested State Inconsistency. State Transition Review is the proposed mitigation category for that weakness: a defensive review of state invariants and authorized transitions. This is a conceptual recommendation without code or operational instructions. It is not evidence of a deployed fix, and it does not establish that every Loom consumer is vulnerable.

sources.title: Fictional Kite tabletop incident
sources.excerpt: Kite Tabletop is a separate invented exercise involving Kite Reserve. It illustrates Stale Rate Acceptance, an abstract weakness assigned to Kite Reserve and its Reed Rates dependency in this scenario. This rate-quality concern is distinct from Nested State Inconsistency in the Harbor exercise. No real oracle, deployed system, attack recipe or measured impact is described.

sources.title: Fictional rate-quality mitigation note
sources.excerpt: Freshness Policy Review is a fictional mitigation category for Stale Rate Acceptance. It calls for defensive evaluation of data freshness requirements and documented failure handling. The note offers no production parameters, implementation code or assurance of effectiveness. It is separate from the State Transition Review proposed for Nested State Inconsistency.
